questions.question: What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?
options: An image is a running app and a container is a file
An image is a read-only package and a container is a running instance of it
They are two names for the same thing
A container is built only from a Maven pom.xml
questions.explanation: The image is the packaged recipe result. Each container is one running copy made from that image.

questions.question: Why does the Dockerfile in this guide use two FROM stages?
options: To run two Spring Boot apps at once
Docker allows only one COPY per stage
To keep build-time files out of the final image
Because Java needs two runtimes
questions.explanation: Only the last stage becomes the image, so files used just for extraction are left behind.

questions.question: A container runs a Spring Boot app on port 8080 inside. The command is: docker run -p 9090:8080 app. Which URL on your laptop reaches the app?
options: http://localhost:8080
http://localhost:9090
http://localhost:80
None, the app cannot be reached
questions.explanation: The -p option is host:container, so host port 9090 forwards to container port 8080.

questions.question: application.properties sets greeting.text=Welcome. application-diwali.properties sets greeting.text=Happy Diwali. The container starts with SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=diwali. What does GET /greeting return?
options: Welcome
Happy Diwali
Both lines
An error
questions.explanation: With the diwali profile active, its property file overrides the default value.

questions.question: docker build fails at the line COPY target/store-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar app.jar with 'file not found'. What is the most likely cause?
options: EXPOSE 8080 is missing
The JAR was never built, so mvn package must run first
ENTRYPOINT must use bash
The image must be named latest
questions.explanation: COPY reads the file from the build folder. If mvn package has not created the JAR, the file does not exist.
